response.text:
Since no significance level is stated, I state the tests at a generic level \(0<\alpha<1\).

## (1) MP test of \(H_0:\theta_1=\theta_2=2\) vs. \(H_1:\theta_1=1,\theta_2=3\)

Under \(H_0\),

\[
f_0(x,y)=4e^{-2x-2y},
\]

and under \(H_1\),

\[
f_1(x,y)=3e^{-x-3y}.
\]

Thus the likelihood ratio is

\[
\frac{f_1(x,y)}{f_0(x,y)}
=
\frac{3}{4}e^{x-y}.
\]

By the Neyman–Pearson lemma, the most powerful level-\(\alpha\) test rejects \(H_0\) for large values of \(f_1/f_0\), equivalently for large values of \(x-y\). Hence the MP test has rejection region

\[
R_\alpha=\{(x,y):x-y>c_\alpha\}.
\]

To choose \(c_\alpha\), note that under \(H_0\), \(X,Y\stackrel{\text{iid}}{\sim}\operatorname{Exp}(2)\). Then \(D=X-Y\) has density

\[
f_D(d)=e^{-2|d|},\qquad -\infty<d<\infty.
\]

Therefore

\[
P_0(D>c)=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac12 e^{-2c}, & c\ge 0,\\[1ex]
1-\dfrac12 e^{2c}, & c<0.
\end{cases}
\]

So \(c_\alpha\) is determined by \(P_0(D>c_\alpha)=\alpha\), namely

\[
c_\alpha=
\begin{cases}
-\dfrac12\log(2\alpha), & 0<\alpha\le \dfrac12,\\[2ex]
\dfrac12\log\{2(1-\alpha)\}, & \dfrac12<\alpha<1.
\end{cases}
\]

Thus the MP level-\(\alpha\) test is

\[
\boxed{\text{Reject }H_0\text{ if }x-y>c_\alpha.}
\]

Equivalently,

\[
\boxed{\text{Reject }H_0\text{ for large }e^{x-y}.}
\]

---

## (2) LRT for \(H_0:\theta_1=\theta_2\) vs. \(H_1:\theta_1\neq\theta_2\)

The likelihood is

\[
L(\theta_1,\theta_2;x,y)
=
\theta_1\theta_2 e^{-\theta_1x-\theta_2y}.
\]

### Unrestricted MLE

Maximizing over \(\theta_1,\theta_2>0\),

\[
\widehat\theta_1=\frac1x,\qquad \widehat\theta_2=\frac1y.
\]

Thus

\[
\sup_{\theta_1,\theta_2}L(\theta_1,\theta_2)
=
\frac1x\frac1y e^{-2}
=
\frac{e^{-2}}{xy}.
\]

### Restricted MLE under \(H_0\)

Under \(H_0\), write \(\theta_1=\theta_2=\theta\). Then

\[
L_0(\theta)=\theta^2 e^{-\theta(x+y)}.
\]

Maximizing,

\[
\widehat\theta_0=\frac{2}{x+y}.
\]

Hence

\[
\sup_{\theta_1=\theta_2}L(\theta_1,\theta_2)
=
\left(\frac{2}{x+y}\right)^2e^{-2}
=
\frac{4e^{-2}}{(x+y)^2}.
\]

Therefore the likelihood ratio statistic is

\[
\Lambda(x,y)
=
\frac{\sup_{\theta_1=\theta_2}L(\theta_1,\theta_2)}
{\sup_{\theta_1,\theta_2}L(\theta_1,\theta_2)}
=
\frac{4e^{-2}/(x+y)^2}{e^{-2}/(xy)}
=
\frac{4xy}{(x+y)^2}.
\]

Let

\[
U=\frac{x}{x+y}.
\]

Then

\[
\frac{y}{x+y}=1-U,
\]

so

\[
\Lambda(x,y)
=
4\frac{x}{x+y}\frac{y}{x+y}
=
4U(1-U).
\]

Thus

\[
\boxed{\Lambda(x,y)=4\frac{x}{x+y}\left(1-\frac{x}{x+y}\right).}
\]

The LRT rejects \(H_0\) for small values of \(\Lambda\), equivalently when \(U=x/(x+y)\) is close to \(0\) or \(1\).

Under \(H_0\), \(X,Y\) are iid exponentials with common rate \(\theta\), and

\[
U=\frac{X}{X+Y}\sim \operatorname{Unif}(0,1).
\]

Therefore the exact level-\(\alpha\) LRT rejects when

\[
U\le \frac{\alpha}{2}
\qquad\text{or}\qquad
U\ge 1-\frac{\alpha}{2}.
\]

Equivalently,

\[
\boxed{\text{Reject }H_0\text{ if }4U(1-U)\le 2\alpha-\alpha^2.}
\]
